fy27.ytd: H1 FY27 (Apr-Sep 2026) domestic PV wholesale 2,637,067 units, +28.3% YoY (Q1 1,273,811 +25.9%; Q2 1,360,687 +30.7%; Sep-26 454,574 +21.8%). UVs ~68% of Q2. Base effect: Sep-25 depressed by pre-GST-2.0 deferral. Dealer inventory 38-40 days (Aug-26) vs 56 a year ago.
fy27.forecast: ICRA: +4-6% wholesale FY27 (reiterated Oct-2026 despite +29% in 5M; high base in H2, price hikes). CRISIL Ratings (May-2026): +5-7% to ~5.9mn units (UV +7-9%, small cars +2-4%); a later Crisil Intelligence note reportedly trimmed to 3-5%. SIAM: ~5-6% (secondhand). Tata Motors PV (Aug-2026): >10% industry growth. RBI hiked repo 25bp to 5.50% on 7-Oct-2026 - downside risk to H2.

drivers.detail: India ~33-34 cars per 1,000 people vs Indonesia ~82-90, China ~221-250, Thailand ~280; ~88% households earn < Rs12 lakh/yr, so affordability caps the addressable base.
UV share rose from 21% (FY16) to ~68% (FY26/H1FY27); hatchback share fell from ~46% peak (FY19) to ~23%. Raises ASPs but erodes Maruti's historic small-car moat; M&M became No.2 in FY26.

Small cars (<4m, petrol <=1200cc/diesel <=1500cc) cut from ~29-31% (28% + cess) to 18% no cess; larger cars 40% flat. Maruti cut prices up to Rs1.29 lakh (~8.5-9% on small cars). Drove record FY26 H2 and +28% H1FY27; Maruti share recovered to ~41%.

Repo cuts in FY26 supported demand, but RBI hiked 25bp to 5.50% on 7-Oct-2026 and moved to 'calibrated tightening' (CPI FY27 5.2%); rate cuts off the table near term - affects auto-loan affordability in H2 FY27.
FADA: rural PV demand grew in line with/above urban in FY27; patchy 2026 monsoon/El Nino named as the single biggest risk; tractors fell 12.6% MoM in Sep-26.

Notified Sep-2026 without separate sub-909kg small-car relief, but reference weight raised (to ~1,229kg) giving a flatter curve that eases targets for lighter cars - seen as net positive for Maruti; still forces CNG/hybrid/EV mix and compliance cost.

EV PV penetration ~2.5% FY25 -> 4.25-4.5% FY26 -> 7.4-7.9% monthly in Jul-Aug 2026; Tata PV expects ~8% by FY27-end. SPMEPCI allows 15% duty on CBU EVs >= $35k CIF (8,000/yr cap) against Rs4,150 cr investment; PM E-DRIVE focuses on 2W/3W/buses/charging. Maruti late (e-Vitara) vs Tata/M&M/MG.
CNG 22% of FY26 PV retail (25% Aug-26), hybrids 8-9%; alt-fuels overtook petrol in Aug-2026. Maruti dominates factory CNG and is strong in strong-hybrids (with Toyota) - a mix tailwind for Maruti.
China's 2025 export licensing curbs forced Maruti to cut Apr-Sep 2025 e-Vitara output ~2/3 (26,500 -> ~8,200); Tata exploring magnet-free motors. No confirmed 2026 normalisation found.

West Asia conflict-linked commodity inflation; Maruti raised prices up to Rs30k (Jun & Aug-2026). Maruti Q1FY27 EBITDA margin 8.6% vs 12.6% (material cost 80.5% vs 74.5% of sales); Hyundai Q1 margin ~9.3% vs 13.3%.
Maruti pays royalty (historically ~5-6% of revenue) and imports some components in yen; a stronger yen raises costs. No 2026-specific quantification found.
India PV exports +17.5% to record ~0.91mn in FY26; Maruti 49% share, 100+ countries; West Asia conflict a risk (12.5% of Maruti exports; Toyota Sep-26 exports -28%).

Share fragmentation: Maruti 51% (FY19) -> 39.3% (FY26, 13-yr low) before H1FY27 rebound; M&M, Tata, Toyota, Kia gaining in SUVs. VinFast Thoothukudi plant (~150k capacity, Rs7,000 cr expansion proposed) with VF6/VF7; BYD/Tesla via imports. Discounting rises when demand slows.

peers.name: Toyota Kirloskar Motor (unlisted)
peers.note: H1FY27 share 6.56% (8.07% H1FY26). Domestic Apr-Jul FY27 128,746 units (+8%); Sep-26 sales -14%, exports -28%. Shares hybrids/badge-engineered models with Maruti.

porter.rivalry: High and rising: top-4 now within ~12-15% share each behind Maruti; SUV launches, discounting and EV price wars fragment share (Maruti 51% FY19 -> ~39-41%).
porter.buyers: Moderate-high: price-sensitive retail buyers with many SUV/CNG/EV choices and easy switching; GST cut and financing availability shape demand, but brand/service network and resale value give incumbents some pricing power.
porter.suppliers: Moderate: fragmented domestic component base, but concentrated inputs (steel, aluminium, PGMs, semiconductors, China-sourced rare-earth magnets and EV cells) have shown pricing and supply leverage in 2025-26.
porter.substitutes: Low-moderate: two-wheelers, used cars, ride-hailing and metro rail substitute at the entry level; within PV, powertrain substitution (CNG/hybrid/EV) shifts value rather than volume.
porter.entrants: Low-moderate: high capex, dealer/service scale and localisation barriers, but SPMEPCI 15% duty route and EV transition lower entry for VinFast, BYD, Tesla and JSW MG.

themes: Volume normalisation after GST-2.0 spike: +28% H1FY27 on a weak base, consensus FY27 4-7% and a tougher FY28 base; RBI tightening (5.50% repo) and monsoon are swing factors.
Small-car revival vs structural SUV shift: GST cut and CAFE-III's flatter curve aid entry cars, but UVs at ~68% keep share pressure on hatchback-heavy portfolios.
Powertrain diversification: CNG (~22-25%), strong hybrids (~8-9%) and EVs (~4% FY26 -> ~8% exit FY27) overtaking petrol; CAFE-III (Apr-2027) makes mix a compliance and margin lever.
Margin squeeze from commodities and geopolitics: steel/aluminium/precious-metal inflation and West Asia conflict cut Q1FY27 EBITDA margins 300-400bp across OEMs; pricing power is the key test.
Export platform scale-up: record ~0.91mn PV exports in FY26 with Maruti ~49%; diversification beyond West Asia, Africa/LatAm growth and EV exports (e-Vitara to Europe/Japan).
Competitive reshuffle and new entrants: M&M/Tata surge, Hyundai slip, VinFast local plant, imported EVs under SPMEPCI; supply-chain localisation (rare-earth magnets, cells) as a differentiator.
